definitionBean.title: Tangent to a Circle
definitionBean.definition: A line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a tangent.
definitionBean.explanation: A tangent touches the circle at only one point, known as the point of contact. The radius drawn to the point of contact is always perpendicular to the tangent, forming a 90° angle.
importantPoints: A tangent touches a circle at only one point
The radius at the point of contact makes an angle of 90° with the tangent
Only one tangent can be drawn to a circle at any point on its circumference
Tangents and radii are perpendicular to each other

definitionBean.title: Properties of Tangents
definitionBean.definition: The lengths of the two tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are always equal.
definitionBean.explanation: If two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle from an external point P, then PA = PB. Furthermore, the line joining the center O to the external point P bisects the angle between the tangents.
importantPoints: Tangents drawn from an external point have equal lengths (PA = PB)
The line joining the center to the external point bisects the angle between tangents
The angle between the tangent and radius is a right angle

parts.statement: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and the distance of Q from the center is 25 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
parts.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the given values from the problem statement.
- Length of the tangent (PQ) = 24 cm
- Distance from the center to point Q (OQ) = 25 cm

Step 2: Apply the geometric theorem regarding tangents and radii.
- We know that the radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.
- Therefore, triangle OPQ is a right-angled triangle at the point of contact, meaning ∠OPQ = 90°.

Step 3: Use the Pythagorean theorem in right triangle OPQ.
- OQ² = OP² + PQ²
- (25)² = OP² + (24)²
- 625 = OP² + 576
- OP² = 625 - 576
- OP² = 49
- OP = 7 cm

Conclusion:
Thus, the radius of the circle is 7 cm.

parts.statement: If TP and TQ are two tangents to a circle with center O such that ∠POQ = 110°, then find ∠PTQ.
parts.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the given information.
- ∠POQ = 110°
- P and Q are points of contact where tangents TP and TQ meet the circle.

Step 2: Recall the radius-tangent perpendicularity property.
- The radius OP is perpendicular to tangent TP, so ∠OPT = 90°.
- The radius OQ is perpendicular to tangent TQ, so ∠OQT = 90°.

Step 3: Use the angle sum property of quadrilateral OPTQ.
- The sum of all interior angles in a quadrilateral is 360°.
- ∠PTQ + ∠OPT + ∠OQT + ∠POQ = 360°
- ∠PTQ + 90° + 90° + 110° = 360°
- ∠PTQ + 290° = 360°
- ∠PTQ = 360° - 290° = 70°

Conclusion:
Thus, the measure of ∠PTQ is 70°.

parts.statement: A tangent PQ at a point P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the center O at a point Q so that OQ = 12 cm. Find the length of PQ.
parts.explanation:
Step 1: List the given parameters.
- Radius of the circle (OP) = 5 cm
- Distance from center to point Q (OQ) = 12 cm

Step 2: State the geometric relation.
- Since PQ is a tangent at point P, radius OP is perpendicular to tangent PQ. Therefore, ∠OPQ = 90°.

Step 3: Apply the Pythagorean theorem in right-angled triangle OPQ.
- OQ² = OP² + PQ²
- 12² = 5² + PQ²
- 144 = 25 + PQ²
- PQ² = 144 - 25 = 119
- PQ = √119 cm

Conclusion:
Thus, the length of PQ is √119 cm.

parts.statement: If PA and PB are two tangents from an external point P to a circle with center O such that ∠APB = 80°, then find ∠POA.
parts.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the symmetry properties of tangents from an external point.
- The line joining the center O to the external point P bisects the angle between the tangents.
- Therefore, ∠APO = (1/2) × ∠APB = (1/2) × 80° = 40°.

Step 2: Use the radius-tangent perpendicularity property.
- Radius OA is perpendicular to tangent PA, so ∠OAP = 90°.

Step 3: Apply the angle sum property in right-angled triangle OAP.
- In triangle OAP, ∠POA + ∠APO + ∠OAP = 180°
- ∠POA + 40° + 90° = 180°
- ∠POA + 130° = 180°
- ∠POA = 180° - 130° = 50°

Conclusion:
Thus, the measure of ∠POA is 50°.
